# technitium_dns_record_mx (Resource)

Manages an MX (mail exchange) record.

Records are matched by zone, name and `preference`, `exchange`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "technitium_dns_record_mx" "primary" {
  zone       = "example.com"
  name       = "@"
  preference = 10
  exchange   = "mail.example.com"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `exchange` (String) Mail server domain name.
- `name` (String) Record name relative to the zone; `@` for the zone apex.
- `preference` (Number) Preference; lower values are tried first.
- `zone` (String) Authoritative zone the record belongs to.

### Optional

- `comments` (String) Free-form comments stored with the record.
- `disabled` (Boolean) Whether the record is disabled (kept but not served).
- `expiry_ttl` (Number) Seconds after the last modification at which the server deletes the record; 0 disables expiry.
- `ttl` (Number) TTL in seconds. Defaults to the server's default record TTL. All records of one type at the same name form an RRset and share a single TTL, so give them the same value.

### Read-Only

- `fqdn` (String) Fully qualified domain name of the record.
- `id` (String) Record identifier and import ID: `<zone>/<name>/<preference> <exchange>`.

## Import

```shell
# <zone>/<name>/<preference> <exchange>
terraform import technitium_dns_record_mx.primary "example.com/@/10 mail.example.com"
```
